1. (S) SITUATION:
USS Nimitz has been badly damaged and Keflavik has been suppressed. NATO has committed its second carrier battle group, centered on USS Enterprise, to hunt down {TaskForceName}. This engagement will determine whether NATO can retain carrier capability in the North Atlantic.
2. (S) MISSION: 2.1 Strike and destroy the USS Enterprise. 2.2 Break the carrier group's ability to conduct sustained operations in the Atlantic. 2.3 {FlagshipName} must survive.
3. (S) EXECUTION: 3.1 Use submarines to approach the carrier group and identify the carrier's position. 3.2 Employ the task force's long-range missiles against Enterprise before the escorts can close. 3.3 Concentrate fires on the carrier first, then disengage or destroy the remaining escorts as the tactical situation permits. 3.4 Preserve the flagship and surviving combat units for the final operation.
4. (S) ENEMY SITUATION: 4.1 USS Enterprise, CVN-65. 4.2 USS Thomas S. Gates, CG-51. 4.3 USS Bunker Hill, CG-52. 4.4 Additional carrier aircraft and escorts are expected.
5. (S) FRIENDLY SITUATION: 5.1 {TaskForceName} is the principal Soviet strike force in the area. 5.2 Assigned submarines are to lead the contact and provide the first attack opportunity.
6. (S) INTEL ASSESSMENT: 6.1 NATO is committed to restoring the initiative after the loss of Nimitz and the suppression of Keflavik. 6.2 Destruction of Enterprise will remove NATO's remaining Atlantic carrier capability. Treat this as the decisive engagement of the campaign.
